publisher_bio: This website was created by Tom Pickup, Reform UK county councillor for Padiham and Burnley West and Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care at Lancashire County Council. He is also parish councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw. Tom builds transparency tools that make public spending data easier to check.

doge_context.political_control_summary: Bradford Council is run by a Reform UK minority administration. After the 7 May 2026 elections the council was in no overall control: Reform UK became the largest party with 29 seats (up from zero), Conservatives 18, Labour 17 (down from a 47-seat majority), Your Bradford Independent group 9, Greens 9, Independents 4, Lib Dems 1; 46 are needed for a majority. At the Annual Council Meeting on 19 May 2026, Cllr Stephen Place (Reform UK) was elected Leader of the Council, carrying the vote after the opposition parties abstained, and formed a six-member all-Reform Executive (Place, Eglin, Birch, Judson, Walker, Morgan).

spend_triangulation.note: Transparency gross = £4.89B across every class in the published corpus. Procurement-paid (discretionary third-party payments) = £4.15B. Non-procurement rows: Care-Act redacted direct payments to individuals (£31.4M), statutory pass-throughs (£695.4K), internal transfers to pension fund / in-house provider / wholly-owned subsidiary (£704.8M) — all excluded from third-party-supplier forensic analyses. Net revenue budget figures (where published) are smaller again because they net capital, grants received, and reserves movements — transparency totals include all of these.

procurement_paid.note: Discretionary third-party supplier payments — the real procurement footprint.

direct_payment_individual.note: Care Act 2014 + UK GDPR redactions — foster carers, SGO recipients, ASC service-user direct-payment holders. Lawfully unnamed.

statutory_pass_through.note: DSG to schools, BCF to NHS ICB, PFI unitary charges, DFG to districts, concessionary travel. Authority has no procurement discretion.

internal_transfer.note: Council's own pension fund, in-house provider arm, or wholly-owned subsidiary. Money from commissioner to provider within the authority boundary.
